claims.text: A Monte Carlo-based sampling scheme can be used to design refractory high-entropy alloy compositions.
Monte Carlo-based sampling can efficiently explore the vast compositional space associated with multi-principal-element alloys.
The proposed sampling scheme can identify intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight RHEA compositions.
Multi-principal-element systems have a very large selection of possible compositions.
The proposed design is intended for high-temperature operating conditions.
The Monte Carlo-based sampling scheme determines or modifies the compositional arrangement of elements.
Statistical-mechanics and thermodynamic principles guide the sampling process.
The sampling process is predicted to identify optimal HEA compositions with improved strength, ductility, and low weight.
Strategies for rapidly determining optimal HEA compositions are currently lacking.
The effectiveness of the method is limited by the accuracy of the statistical-mechanics and thermodynamic principles employed.
The complexity of compositional space creates uncertainty in the accuracy of the predicted outcomes.
